newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures end firmer but still in range.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures end firmer but still in range.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed mostly firmer on Tuesday, but prices were still seen locked in a range.
July ended up six stg at 1,025 stg per tonne with September gaining four to 1,041. Total futures volume stood at 4,273 contracts and options traded 1,050 times.
According to LIFFE, 500 May 1,050 stg calls, 500 May 1,025 calls and 50 September 1,200 calls changed hands.
Traders said a local crossed the options and then crossed about 500 March and May 1998 futures in the afternoon.
Another firm also crossed July/March 1998 at 20 stg, they said. Traders also saw some activity on the July/September switch at 18 stg, but they said that activity was light.
Traders said the slight up move in cocoa came mostly from light trade buying. A large trade house bought July to account for most of the 1,681 contracts traded in that month.
In the morning, a large, privately-held U.S. firm bought 100 to 150 September contracts, traders said.
Prices had little reaction to a drop in German cocoa imports to 15,263 tonnes in January.

Despite some scattered buying, traders said the market was still mostly rangebound. Without fresh news and momentum either way in the market, they expected July to stay trapped in a wide range between about 1,060 and the April 9 low of 980.
